answer:
For positive score $s_+$ and candidates $s_j$, InfoNCE is $L=-s_+/\tau+\log\sum_j e^{s_j/\tau}$. Its score derivative is $(p_j-\mathbf1[j=+])/\tau$. Lower temperature concentrates probability on high-scoring candidates and magnifies mistakes involving hard negatives. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084)

As $\tau\to0$, log-sum-exp approaches the maximum score after appropriate scaling. If a negative beats the positive, it dominates the gradient; if the positive wins by a fixed margin, the exponential suppression can make gradients vanish despite the $1/\tau$ factor. Ties require separate treatment. Very low temperatures amplify false negatives and numerical sensitivity. Choose temperature using retrieval quality and representation diagnostics, with stable log-sum-exp and an explicit treatment of duplicate positives.
